subject: Post-demo: data handling & telemetry vendor checklist for Finlytics
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Kyle Nguyen <kyle@finlytics.ai>, Privacy Team <privacy@finlytics.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 31 Jul 2026 15:20:00 +0000
Subject: Post-demo: quick recap and a few follow-ups on telemetry / data handling

Hi Kyle — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and the things we discussed that we'll follow up on: 

1) Primary ask: which categories of PII (if any) might transit Redwood in your workflows (examples: email, customer name, payment tokens, account IDs)?
2) Data residency preference: you mentioned EU-only for production — can you confirm whether dev/staging may remain in us-east?
3) Logging & retention: target retention window for request/response logs and any auditing needs (SLA for log access)
4) Third-party telemetry: you asked for the list of telemetry vendors we surface and what data they receive (aggregated metrics vs. request-level telemetry)

Next steps I propose: I will attach a short telemetry vendor questionnaire and our data residency options; Ben (SE) will draft answers for the Telemetry checklist and Laura (security) will confirm residency/KMS options. Can we target early next week for a follow-up call?

Attachments: TelemetryVendor_Questionnaire.pdf, DataResidency_RegionOptions.pdf

Thanks — Camila

Date: Sat, 01 Aug 2026 09:10:12 +0000
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap and a few follow-ups on telemetry / data handling

Thanks Camila — great walk-through. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII scope: we try to avoid storing direct payment tokens or full SSNs. Primary identifiers we pass into APIs today are customer_id (internal GUID), user_email (hashed in some pipelines, plain in others), and occasionally name+company for enrichment flows. We need confirmation whether Redwood ever persists raw request bodies in telemetry logs by default.
- Residency: production must be EU-only (we're bound by a regional hosting clause in our contract). Non-prod can be EU or us-east, but we'd prefer EU if feasible.
- Retention: compliance requires retaining audit logs for 12 months and ability to export on request within 48 hours.
- Telemetry vendors: curious what you send to internal telemetry/observability vendors. Specifically: do those vendors ever receive request-level content (token-level or prompt text), or only aggregated metrics and sampling?

Samir Rao at TelemetryCo (cc'd in a later thread) asked whether Redwood's marketplace integrations ever route customer data through partner accounts — we need clarity on that flow.

We can do a follow-up on Tue/Wed. Appetite to have Ben and your security lead on the call.

-Kyle

Head of Product, Finlytics AI

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Camila / Laura — quick draft answers and action items below. I'm happy to refine before we send to Finlytics.

1) Do we persist raw request bodies in telemetry logs?
- Short answer: No by default. Our runtime writes minimal request metadata (latency, error codes, model version, hashed request id) to internal metrics. For customers who opt into deep debug logging, request/response bodies are stored in an encrypted log bucket for a limited window (configurable).
- Action: add a note that this is an opt-in debug feature and can be disabled per-customer at provisioning. (Action owner: Ben)

2) Telemetry vendors / third-parties
- We use an internal observability pipeline and ship aggregated metrics to third-party telemetry vendors (TelemetryCo) for dashboards and alerting. We do NOT send continuous request-level prompt text or full token streams to vendors. Sampling for traces is configurable; default is 0.1% for request-level payloads.
- We can provide a vendor whitelist + dataflow diagram under NDA. (Action owner: Camila to share diagram link)

3) Data residency & KMS
- EU-only production: supported via our Private/VPC deployment option or by pinning region in Dedicated for enterprise customers. Customer-managed KMS is supported in our Private offering (we integrate with AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS and HSMs).
- Retention: we support configurable logging retention; default platform retention is 90 days, enterprise customers can request 12 months via contract addendum. We can provide automated export tooling for e-discovery requests within 48 hours. (Action owner: Laura to confirm timelines and SLA language)

4) Marketplace / partner flow question
- Marketplace integrations are thin: customers authorize and we exchange minimal metadata for billing. We DO NOT route customer prompt/response payloads through partner accounts as part of marketplace provisioning. We'll prepare a short note to certify that.

Proposed next steps: finalize the TelemetryVendor_Questionnaire with exact sampling figures and redact examples, Laura to attach SOC2 extract and confirm export SLA, Camila to send follow-up calendar invite for Tue 2026-08-04 15:00 UTC.
